nodes.label: ComLinked AI Lead Agent - Task Document & Process Specification
AI Lead Agent
nodes.rationale: Finds the right customer, vendor, supplier or partner, talks to the matched company's agent, qualifies the fit and books a virtual meeting only at 75+/100. SME members lack time and know-how to generate leads; community managers do this matching by hand today, and the agent does it continuously without headcount, fitting an AI-first operating model. It never signs, quotes binding prices or commits either company; people make every commitment.

nodes.label: Mandate
nodes.rationale: Written mandate the company sets up and its approvers own; defines what the agent may do alone, with approval, or never. Set up at stage 0 (Ideal Partner Profile per match type, approver roles, disclosure tiers, calendar, outreach limits).

nodes.label: Approver roles (Owner/Admin, Sales Lead, Procurement Lead, Meeting attendee)
nodes.rationale: Roles approve confidential sharing and meetings per match type. If no role-holder responds within one business day, one reminder; after a second day escalate to Owner/Admin. Silence is never treated as approval.

nodes.label: Agent data sources
nodes.rationale: ComLinked profile (Tier 0), ComDash activity and behaviour signals (internal only, never quoted to another agent), public web data (Tier 0, conflicts flagged to owner), and private uploads (default Tier 2 until marked shareable). Search scope is the member's own chamber by default; every fact used in a score is recorded with its source.

nodes.label: End-to-end workflow (10 stages, 2 human gates)
nodes.rationale: Mandate set-up, discover, desk score and shortlist, engage, qualify, Gate A, final score, Gate B, book and hand off, outcome and learning. The agent runs on its own except at the two gates; every meeting outcome feeds back into scoring.

nodes.label: Gate A: confidential disclosure approval
nodes.rationale: When either agent needs Tier 2 information, approval is requested per item from the right approver; only what is approved is shared.

nodes.label: Gate B: meeting confirmation
nodes.rationale: At score 75+, the agent proposes 3 slots from calendar free/busy and both sides' approvers must confirm before the invite goes out.

nodes.label: Score bands (Book 75-100, Nurture 60-74, Drop under 60)
nodes.rationale: Book goes to Gate B; Nurture shows the match in ComDash with its gaps and re-checks in 30 days or on profile change; Drop logs the reason and does not contact again for 90 days.

nodes.label: Agent task catalogue (T01-T18)
nodes.rationale: Discrete tools or jobs the agent can run: build IPP, discover, enrich, desk score, knock-outs, open/respond to engagement, qualification exchange, disclosure approval, final score, propose/confirm/book meeting, handoff package, claim-your-profile outreach, capture outcome, nurture re-check, escalate to human.

nodes.label: T15 Claim-your-profile outreach
nodes.rationale: When the best match has no claimed profile, sends a CASL-compliant email with a match teaser (match type and why, no confidential details); 14-day window with one reminder at day 7, then park. The agent recruits the company into the network rather than skipping it.

nodes.label: T16 Capture outcome
nodes.rationale: 24 hours after the meeting asks each side: proceed, follow up later, or not a fit; logs the reason and recalibrates scoring.

nodes.label: ComLinked Match and Qualification Scorecard
nodes.rationale: Scored out of 100 across seven categories: need and offer fit 25, capacity and commercial fit 15, proximity and logistics 10, credibility and trust 15, intent and timing 15, relationship and network 10 (desk score max 90, before contact), agent qualification outcome 10 (after agents talk). Weights tunable per match type and versioned so reports cite the scorecard version. Honest labelling: called a match score, not a probability, until about 200 completed meetings calibrate it.

nodes.label: Knock-outs
nodes.rationale: Block contact whatever the score: either company opted out, 90-day cool-off after a decline, open compliance or conduct flag, declared exclusivity conflict, or an inactive profile.

nodes.label: Agent-to-agent communication protocol
nodes.rationale: Plain-language messages wrapped in a structured envelope (engagement ID, sender/receiver agent and company, message type, disclosure tier, timestamp, text), stored append-only. Types: INTRO, MANDATE_CHECK, QUALIFY_Q/QUALIFY_A, DISCLOSURE_PENDING, DISCLOSURE_GRANT/DECLINE, MEETING_PROPOSAL, MEETING_ACCEPT, MEETING_BOOKED, ESCALATE, CLOSE. Rules: INTRO states it is an AI agent, answer only from own company's data, decline or escalate off-mandate questions, 20-turn cap per side, figures labelled indicative and non-binding.

nodes.label: Disclosure tiers (0 Public, 1 Shareable, 2 Confidential, 3 Never)
nodes.rationale: Tier 0 shared freely; Tier 1 freely within the mandate; Tier 2 (prices, volumes, customer names, specs, plans) only after per-item approval; Tier 3 (contracts, banking, tax IDs, staff personal data, third-party information) never.

nodes.label: Free inbound-only agent
nodes.rationale: Every claimed profile gets a free inbound-only agent that can answer and accept engagements; only outbound prospecting is paid. This keeps the network full of agents to talk to. Parked matches are re-checked if the company later claims or switches its agent on.

nodes.label: Meeting booking rules
nodes.rationale: Reads only free/busy, never event details; proposes 3 slots within 5-10 business days in Eastern Time; virtual 30 or 45 minutes on Google Meet or Microsoft Teams via the connected Google or Outlook calendar; both approvers confirm first; reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before.

nodes.label: Handoff package (transcript, agenda, selection report)
nodes.rationale: Attached to the invite and saved in both companies' ComDash: full agent-to-agent transcript with approvals marked, a timed agenda with pre-meeting actions and next steps, and a selection report covering the scorecard breakdown, evidence and sources, runner-up candidates and risks.

nodes.label: CASL outreach email compliance
nodes.rationale: Legal risk sits with off-platform emails (mainly claim-your-profile emails to scraped companies). Implied consent under the conspicuous-publication rule needs all three elements proven per message, so store the source URL, a page capture showing no opt-out statement, the recipient's role and a relevance reason; identify ComLinked and the member, give a mailing address, one-click unsubscribe honoured within 10 business days; skip generic addresses from directories with no-solicitation disclaimers.

nodes.label: PIPEDA personal information rules
nodes.rationale: Limit agent use of personal information to business contact information for work communication; keep transcripts only as long as needed (24 months suggested) with company export/delete; publish a plain-language notice and name a privacy officer.

nodes.label: AI transparency
nodes.rationale: Every agent message states it comes from an AI agent and names the company it represents; every handoff package notes which parts were AI-generated.

nodes.label: Rate limits and anti-spam rules
nodes.rationale: Outbound engagements set by tier; 1 follow-up per unanswered engagement; 90-day cool-off after a decline; 2 claim emails per unclaimed company per 90 days across all members; inbound capped by receiver (default 10/week); 20 turns per side. Outbound pauses if decline and opt-out rate exceeds 30% over 20 engagements until the Owner reviews the mandate.

nodes.label: Monetization tiers (Member, Growth, Pro, Enterprise / Chamber Partner)
nodes.rationale: Paid upgrade priced by agent-led outbound engagements per month (placeholder CAD): Member $0 inbound-only, Growth $79 / 10, Pro $199 / 40 with cross-chamber add-on, Enterprise custom. Inbound answering is free because the network needs agents on both sides; chamber revenue share applies to all paid tiers. Pilot suggestion: 3 months of Growth free for PCCC members, converting in April 2027.

nodes.label: PCCC (Philippine Canadian Chamber of Commerce) pilot
nodes.rationale: Agent specified for the PCCC pilot launching January 1, 2027 with about 500 members in year one; designed to scale to every chamber.

nodes.label: Simulation A: Kusina Express Foods x NorthPack Solutions supplier match
nodes.rationale: Fictional worked example: 14 packaging companies scored, 5 pass knock-outs, top three engaged (NorthPack 77/90, GreenForm 62/90, Pacific Rim 61/90); NorthPack qualifies at 86/100 after a Gate A price-range approval and Gate B approvals on both sides; 45-minute Google Meet booked for January 20, 2027 with full agenda and selection report; GreenForm (66) and Pacific Rim (64) kept in Nurture.

nodes.label: Simulations B-D: customer, vendor and partner matches
nodes.rationale: B: Bayanihan Clean Co. and Lakeshore Dental Group (unclaimed profile, claim email first, 81/100); C: Sampaguita Home Care and ShiftWise Software (Gate A on staff numbers and budget, 78/100); D: Tala Travel & Tours and Bagong Simula Settlement Services (cross-chamber search Manitoba to PCCC, 77/100).

nodes.label: Model for language, services for rules
nodes.rationale: Build the agent as a language model for conversation and judgement wrapped in deterministic platform services that enforce scoring, disclosure, approvals and rate limits; the model never decides on its own whether something may be shared or booked. Tool-based actions check tier, approval and rate limits; one agent instance per company per engagement so no conversation sees another company's data; everything logged append-only to produce the transcript.

nodes.label: Agent core data entities
nodes.rationale: Mandate, IdealPartnerProfile, Candidate, Engagement, AgentMessage, DisclosureItem, ApprovalRequest, ScoreRecord, Meeting, HandoffPackage, ConsentRecord, Outcome, each mapped to task IDs.

nodes.label: IdealPartnerProfile
nodes.rationale: Match type, criteria, ranges, exclusions; built per match type at mandate set-up (T01) and used for discovery (T02).

nodes.label: Engagement
nodes.rationale: Initiator, counterparty, status, band, turn count. One outbound conversation opened with a counterparty agent or human counts as one engagement for billing; inbound and claim emails do not.

nodes.label: ConsentRecord
nodes.rationale: Address, source URL, page capture, role, relevance reason; evidence for CASL implied consent on claim-your-profile outreach (T15).

nodes.label: Agent pilot KPIs
nodes.rationale: Placeholder targets: engagement-to-meeting 15%, meeting-to-opportunity 40%, approval turnaround under 4 business hours, opt-out under 10%, profile claim rate 20%, agent adoption 50% of PCCC members by month 6.

nodes.label: Open decisions for ComLinked (AI Lead Agent)
nodes.rationale: Final tier prices and limits; legal review of CASL consent records and PIPEDA notice; whether counterparties see the initiator's score; transcript retention period; chamber revenue share percentage; whether Gate A can be pre-approved for repeat disclosures.

nodes.label: CRTC: Guidance on implied consent under CASL
BLG: Federal Court of Appeal rules CASL constitutionally valid (2020)
Slaw: Overview of PIPEDA amendments, business contact information
